Marrow oedema (T1 low, STIR high), cortical breach, subperiosteal/soft-tissue abscess with rim enhancement – earliest diagnosis.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Osteomyelitis (US)

Subperiosteal fluid collection, periosteal elevation, soft-tissue oedema (child).

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Osteomyelitis

Bone infection: early X-ray normal (10–14 d), then osteolysis + periosteal reaction; chronic: diffuse diaphyseal sclerosis, thickened cortex, sequestrum. MRI best early.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Bone tuberculosis

Osteolysis with little sclerosis or periosteal reaction, osteoporosis, soft-tissue (cold) abscess; spine most frequent (Pott).

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Osteoma

Dense, round, well-delineated ivory opacity – skull, paranasal (frontal/ethmoid) sinuses. Benign.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Bone cyst

Well-delineated central lytic lesion of the metaphysis in a child/adolescent, thin sclerotic rim, cortical thinning ± "fallen fragment" after fracture (simple bone cyst).

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Enchondroma

Central lucent lesion in a short tubular bone (hands), lobulated, endosteal scalloping, ring-and-arc chondroid calcifications, no periosteal reaction.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Chondrosarcoma

Adult (> 40 y), pelvis/proximal femur: lytic lesion with ring-and-arc "popcorn/snowflake" chondroid calcifications, endosteal scalloping, soft-tissue mass.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Plasmocytoma / myeloma

Multiple sharply delineated round/oval "punched-out" osteolyses without sclerotic rim (skull "raindrop", axial skeleton) – myeloma; single = plasmocytoma.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Bone metastases

Sclerotic ("ivory") vertebra – osteoblastic metastasis (prostate, breast) or lymphoma; lytic metastases: lung, kidney, thyroid.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Osteogenic osteosarcoma

Sclerotic (bone-forming) aggressive metaphyseal lesion with "sunburst" spiculated periosteal reaction and Codman triangle.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.

Bilateral symmetric sacroiliitis (erosions, subchondral sclerosis → ankylosis); spine: shiny corners, square vertebrae, thin vertical syndesmophytes → "bamboo spine", calcified ligaments ("railway / tram line"), osteoporosis.

Knee osteoarthritis: (medial) joint-space narrowing without fusion, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Osteochondroma

Metaphyseal exostosis pointing away from the joint; cortex and medulla continuous with the host bone; cartilage cap (MRI). Risk: chondrosarcoma.

q: What is the diagnosis? Name the technique and the key sign.
a:
Rheumatoid arthritis

Symmetric small-joint arthritis: soft-tissue swelling, periarticular osteoporosis, marginal erosions, subchondral cysts, uniform narrowing → subluxation, ulnar deviation, ankylosis (stages I–IV). US/Doppler: synovial thickening with hyperaemia.
